## Extraction ledger — COMPLETE. Closing.

All 3 FAILs, the 4 PARTIALs' actionable halves and the checklist-maintenance list extracted. Every defect re-verified live on `origin/main` — **none already-fixed**, no duplicates.

| Run item | Finding | Card | Lane |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `admin-lifecycle-operations` | `remove-user` is **non-atomic and can never succeed** — a 409 `DELETE_RESTRICTED` leaks as a bodyless 500, credentials are already deleted and **not rolled back**, leaving an un-authenticatable identity on the roster | #7724 | `domain:identity` |
| — same item, second half | impersonation is invisible in the console: no banner, no "Stop impersonating", no entry point | objectstack-ai/objectui#4304 | objectui |
| `invitation-scope-gates` (a) | `accept-invitation` → bodyless 500, the row stays `pending` forever — acceptance re-inserts a membership the sign-up reconciler already created | #7725 | `domain:identity` |
| `invitation-scope-gates` (b) | `cancel-invitation` writes `status:'canceled'`, absent from the spec's 4-value `InvitationStatus` enum | #7726 | `domain:spec` |
| `api-key-ui-lifecycle` | **API keys cannot be revoked through any product route** — the object declares revoke/restore as `PATCH` while the same file sets `apiMethods:['get','list']` (405) | #7727 | `security` · `domain:metadata` |
| — same item, secondary | `sys_api_key.key` (a SHA-256 hash) serializes over the data API despite its "never exposed to clients" description | #7728 | `domain:metadata` |
| `teams-bu-membership` (PARTIAL) | **sharing-rule revocation is lazy** — rebind triggers bind to the rule's own object, never to `sys_business_unit(_member)`, so a BU moved *out* of a shared subtree keeps read access until the record is next written | #7729 | `security` · `domain:identity` |
| `session-list-revoke` (PARTIAL) | `sys_session.revoked_at`/`revoke_reason` — the ADR-0069 D4 revoke-audit trail is effectively inert | #7732 | `domain:identity` |
| `auth-method-matrix` (PARTIAL) | `change-email` / `delete-user` are booked as mounted in `auth-route-ledger.ts` but plugin-auth never configures better-auth's `user.changeEmail`/`user.deleteUser` — no switch to enable them | #7735 | `domain:identity` |
| Checklist maintenance ×5 | role vocabulary, invitation clause 6, admin-lifecycle clause 4 oracle, teams-bu `knownGap`, import-wizard fixture note | #7740 | `domain:devx` |

The 5 PASS items and the 2 ledger-BLOCKED items produced no cards.

### One place the extraction is more accurate than the run

**#7732** — the run reported `revoked_at`/`revoke_reason` as having "no writer anywhere in the tree". Measured: `auth-manager.ts` **does** stamp both on three paths (idle timeout, absolute-max, concurrent-cap; `:4606`/`:4647`, present at the served pin too — not a post-pin fix). The defect is narrower and more precise than stated: the **admin/interactive** revoke path *deletes* the row rather than tombstoning, and GC removes expired ones, so the audit trail is **effectively** inert rather than never-written. The card says so, because "no writer" would have sent a dev looking for the wrong thing.

### Two of these are security-relevant and neither is a bypass

Worth stating so nobody over- or under-escalates:

- **#7727** — a leaked API key **cannot be revoked without direct database access**. The run filed it publicly on the reasoning that a dead feature grants an attacker nothing they don't already have; enforcement of the flag itself is fine (setting `revoked=1` out-of-band 401s the very next call). The fix is to allow `update` scoped to `revoked`, or to give revoke/restore a real route.
- **#7729** — the risky direction is **revocation**, not grant: after a business unit is re-parented *out* of a shared subtree, its members keep read access until the shared record is next written. The measured matrix (`inSubtree=1`, `reparentedOut(no touch)=1`, `reparentedOut(touched)=0`) is in the card.

### An environment fact that shaped the whole area, worth keeping

The seeded dev admin is promoted to the ObjectStack **platform** admin but its better-auth `sys_user.role` stays `'user'` — so the entire better-auth-native admin family 403s out of the box. The runner provisioned a genuine admin with one system-context write to its own throwaway DB rather than record six `blocked`, which is why this area has real coverage instead of a wall of skips. Recorded in #7740 so the next sweep does not re-derive it.

Provenance: maintainer standing rule that every QA problem becomes an issue; run records close at extraction, same exit as #7514/#7463/#7627.
